events.text:
**Recommendation: fish Grand Haven. I'd rate it 1 out of 4, the best of four weak options.** Cast glow spoons at dawn and dusk. None of the four ports looks better than "below average" for pier salmon this week.

| Port | My rating | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| Grand Haven | 1 (below average, upper end) | Medium |
| Muskegon | 1 | Low (no pier reports) |
| South Haven | 1 | Low (no pier reports) |
| St. Joseph | 0 (slow) | Medium |

**What the reports say** (newest reports are from 2023-08-30, 6 days old)
- **Grand Haven** is the only port with pier salmon catches in each of the last four weeks.
  - "Pier anglers caught a few salmon while casting spoons in low light conditions" (quality 1, Grand Haven, 2023-08-30).
  - A few salmon were caught off the piers on glow spoons (quality 1, Grand Haven, 2023-08-23).
  - Pier anglers casting glow spoons and plugs found the salmon bite slow (quality 0, Grand Haven, 2023-08-16).
  - A few salmon were caught on glow plugs (quality 1, Grand Haven, 2023-08-02).
  - Boats were doing well close to shore, with good action in 40–80 ft of water on glow or chrome J-plugs and white flasher/flies (quality 3, Grand Haven, 2023-08-30).
- **Muskegon** had no pier salmon reports in the last eight weeks.
  - Boats called salmon slow, with the most success 55–100 ft down in 70–130 ft of water (quality 0, Muskegon, 2023-08-30).
  - The week before, the salmon action had "slowed down" (Muskegon, 2023-08-23).
- **South Haven** had no pier salmon reports in the last eight weeks.
  - Boats were rated slow (quality 0) in 90–120 ft of water. The report text says fishing was "pretty good" for the boats that got out, and the Black River trolling was "very slow" (South Haven, 2023-08-30).
  - The week before, fish were "very scattered" (South Haven, 2023-08-23).
- **St. Joseph** had pier fishing that was slow. "Pier anglers who targeted trout and salmon had slow fishing" (quality 0, St. Joseph, 2023-08-30). Few boats got out because of poor weather (St. Joseph, 2023-08-30). The earlier pier report was also weak: a few coho on nightcrawlers and some steelhead on shrimp (quality 1, St. Joseph, 2023-08-09).

**Water**
- The buoy summary for the week before today shows surface temperatures of St. Joseph 71 F (+4 F), South Haven 68 F (+5 F) and Grand Haven/Muskegon 63 F (+12 F). These are measured.
- The 2023-08-30 reports flagged a possible upwelling, a sharp surface drop, at Grand Haven and Muskegon (−11 F). That is the pattern that can bring salmon toward the piers (Michigan Sea Grant/MSU Extension, general guidance).
- The +12 F this past week suggests the water at Grand Haven and Muskegon has warmed back up, though I can't tell from the summary how much.
- The tool gave no wind forecast, no modeled pierhead temperatures and no cold-layer depths, so I can't tell you whether a fresh upwelling is under way.

**History (same time of year, 2022)**
- Early September pier fishing was slow for salmon at Grand Haven (quality 0 on 2022-09-07 and 2022-09-14) and Muskegon (quality 0, "No salmon were reported from the breakwalls," 2022-09-07).
- There were no pier reports for South Haven or St. Joseph in those weeks. Only a couple of boats fishing the pier heads at St. Joseph caught a few coho and Chinook (2022-09-14).
- Pier fishing is usually slow in early September and tends to improve later in the fall. That is my general impression of the pattern, not something these reports state.

**My read**
- I'd expect Grand Haven to give a few fish at best, mostly at first and last light. Boats were finding salmon close to shore there, in 40–80 ft, so fish are near the pier.
- I'd expect Muskegon to be about the same. Its coldest water is a plus, but its boat reports were slow.
- I'd expect South Haven and St. Joseph to be weaker. Their water is warmer, and St. Joseph's pier report was slow.
- Treat the Muskegon and South Haven ratings as guesses, because there are no pier data for them.
- If you see a north or east wind, or a sharp drop in water temperature at the pier, that is the best sign to move up a rating point.
